evals.prompt: Show me an ESIMD kernel for an Intel Arc B580 (Xe2) that computes the sum of each row of an fp32 matrix [512 x 16384]. Use one work-group of 16 threads per row: each thread sums its share of the row, then the 16 partial sums are combined through shared local memory.
evals.expected_output: An ESIMD kernel launched with an nd_range of 16 work-items per work-group. It calls slm_init with a size covering the 16 partial sums at the start of the kernel, each thread writes its partial sum at a byte offset (for example lid * sizeof(float)), and a barrier() that every thread reaches separates the writes from the reads. The partials are read back with an SLM block load and reduced with an ESIMD reduction.

evals.prompt: What is the largest slm_init size I can use in an ESIMD kernel on an Intel Arc B580, and what happens if I ask for more?
evals.expected_output: The limit is device-specific: query sycl::info::device::local_mem_size (an Arc B580 reports 128 KB per work-group) rather than assuming a number. With ahead-of-time compilation, a larger slm_init fails at build time with 'SLM size exceeds target limits'. Large allocations also reduce how many work-groups can be resident on an Xe core, so use the smallest size the algorithm needs.
